note: Real-world regression case. Each entry is one defect or one false alarm seen on a production TypeScript dictionary. status: currently-caught = check.mjs reports it today on json/ and must keep doing so. known-gap = the skill misses it (or mis-reports it) today. fix = item number in the fix plan. layer: checker = check.mjs should decide it; agent = needs the SKILL.md read-through, the audit checklist, or lookup.mjs. Suggested replacements are drafts, not a native-speaker review.

fixPlan.1: Read typed TS/JS dictionaries with functions (adapter) and fix the dead-end error message
fixPlan.2: Allowlist / config for deliberate omissions and kept-English terms
fixPlan.3: Group possible-source-copy by section and print a coverage summary
fixPlan.4: New mechanical checks (count order, placeholder spacing, stale, terminology, English in branches, English residue, invisible characters)
fixPlan.5: Too-strict checks and misleading notes (dropped repeated placeholder, length-blowup, Indonesian Daftar)
fixPlan.6: Locale notes (th, vi, fil, ko, te; ta.md garbled sentence; ms generic error)
fixPlan.7: Audit checklist as testable patterns; installed-copy test path
fixPlan.8: Severity buckets and grouped summary in the report

'{noun} (s)' left from the English '{noun}(s)'. Vietnamese '(các)' and Filipino '(mga)' are the native equivalents and are fine. Tamil '(கள்)' is also native.

U+200B zero-width spaces inside 'sử dụng' and 'kiến thức', a known machine-translation paste artifact. 18 strings in the real catalog (vi 13, ta 3, ar 2). Exempt ZWNJ/ZWJ where the script needs them (fa, hi, ml, si...).
Source uses `n === 1 ? ... : ...` and `${count === 1 ? '' : 's'}`. Arabic needs six categories; the target has one form. Visible only in the TS source, so it belongs to the adapter or scan.mjs.
